correctness.rationale: The full factor-length polynomial follows from the mutually exclusive 1-, 2-, 3-, 4-run classification, with Q the union of two finite integer rectangles and 4-run complementary pairs impossible. Replacing z by 1 yields the stated exact closed formula. For equal middle lengths t the half-count is max(t,min(a,d))+t(min(a,t)+min(d,t)), bounded by t(n-2t+1) with equality precisely a,d<=t. For unequal lengths, reversal-complement reduces to b<c and the two cases d>=b and d<b both yield C/2<=n^2/8. The integer quadratic and direct n=4,5 cases prove sharp bounds and all maximizers. A separate literal factor enumerator compared every polynomial coefficient for 2401 quadruples and checked all exact maxima/equalities at lengths 4..64. No finite enumeration is used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: Currie et al. explicitly study the total number of complemented words as a meaningful avoidance parameter. The four-run family is the first small-run setting where two distinct 01 borders and a 10 border combine into a two-rectangle union, and a three-run complementary pair exists exactly when interior run lengths agree. The theorem simultaneously gives a complete per-length spectrum, an exact four-variable count, a finite-n sharp extremum, and all maximizing run quadruples. Unequal interior runs suffer a proved additive gap of order n, revealing a structural resonance not accounted for by routine monotonicity or a trivial bound. This is a natural completed finite classification with a plausible role as a base case for more-run complement-factor theory. Limits: no general high-run theorem and no independent assessment.
